chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'mmar ibn Khallad, who said:
I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was saying: 'The trustworthy one does not betray you, but you trusted the untrustworthy one.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reason for betrayal according to Imam Al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: This concise maxim from Imam al-Rida (AS), transmitted through the chain of Shaykh al-Kulayni, clarifies the psychological and spiritual mechanics of betrayal by distinguishing between the inherent nature of the trustee and the act of entrustment. It serves as a practical ethical guideline in Shia jurisprudence and character development, advising believers to verify the 'amanah' (trustworthiness) of individuals before delegating responsibilities, rather than blaming the trustworthy for the failures of the untrustworthy. This principle underscores the importance of discernment (tadabbur) in social and administrative interactions within the community.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Mo’mar Bin Khallad who said,
‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Abu ja’far<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘The trustworthy did not betray you, but you trusted the untrustworthy one’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Mu’ammar ibn Khallad who has said the following: “
I once heard abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say, “A trustworthy person has not betrayed you but you have trusted a treacherous one.’”
